payload.raw_reference: Maryland  State  Department  of  Education  (MSDE)  Maryland  K-12 Artificial Intelligence Guidance

payload.text: It is the policy of the Board that artificial intelligence be used only in ways that enhance, and never replace,  the  professional  judgment  of  educators,  counselors,  and  school  leaders.

All artificial intelligence used by [Name] County Public Schools ([NCPS]) must serve clear educational or operational purposes, protect the rights and safety of students and staff, and comply with all applicable federal and Maryland law.
payload.binds: All artificial intelligence used by [Name] County Public Schools ([NCPS])

payload.text: This policy directs the Superintendent to establish administrative regulations that implement these expectations in instruction, assessment, professional learning, procurement, data governance, and operations.
Computer systems that perform tasks commonly associated with human intelligence, such as recognizing patterns, generating content, making predictions, or recommending actions.
A category of artificial intelligence that produces new content, including text, images, audio, code, or video, in response to user prompts.

The knowledge and skills needed to understand how artificial intelligence systems work, evaluate their outputs for accuracy and bias, recognize appropriate and inappropriate uses, and apply ethical judgment when using these systems.
The use of an artificial intelligence system to produce a recommendation, score, classification, or decision that affects a student or employee, with or without human involvement.
Any use of artificial intelligence that affects student access to programs, services, opportunities, discipline, evaluation, or the protection of civil rights.
Consequential uses require documented human oversight.

Meaningful review by a qualified employee who has the authority and information needed to interpret, contextualize, override, or reject an artificial intelligence output before it affects a student or employee.
Information that, alone or in combination, can be used to identify a specific student or employee, as defined under applicable federal and Maryland law.
Artificial  intelligence  shall  support,  not  replace,  professional  educators  and  staff.
Any  artificial intelligence  output  used  in  a  consequential  decision  affecting  a  student  or  employee  shall  be subject  to  documented  human  oversight.
Employees retain  the  authority  and  responsibility  to interpret, contextualize, override, or reject artificial intelligence recommendations.
Artificial intelligence tools may be used only for approved educational and operational purposes consistent with this policy and its administrative regulations.
Entering personally identifiable student or employee information into generative artificial intelligence tools that are not approved and contractually protected by [NCPS];
Using artificial intelligence to make a final consequential decision about a student or employee without human review;
Collecting biometric, behavioral, or location data through artificial intelligence systems unless legally required, educationally justified, and approved by [NCPS];
Using artificial intelligence in any manner that violates [NCPS] policies, the student or employee codes of conduct, or applicable law.

All  artificial  intelligence  use  shall  comply  with  applicable  privacy  and  data  protection  laws, including the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA), the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA), the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment (PPRA), and the Maryland Student  Data  Privacy  Act.

payload.raw_reference: Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)

payload.text: [NCPS]  shall  minimize  the  data  shared  with  artificial  intelligence systems,  maintain  strong  cybersecurity  protections,  and  require  human  oversight  of  artificial intelligence systems that process student or employee data.
Artificial  intelligence  shall  be  used  to  expand,  not  restrict,  equitable  access  to  high-quality learning.

All artificial intelligence use shall comply with federal and state civil rights laws, including Title VI, Title IX, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), and  the  Individuals  with  Disabilities  Education  Act  (IDEA).
Artificial  intelligence  may  support accessibility  but  shall  not  replace  legally  required  evaluations,  services,  accommodations,  or language  access.
[NCPS]  shall  monitor  artificial  intelligence  tools  for  biased  or  inequitable outcomes and take corrective action where disparities emerge.
payload.mechanism_stated: take corrective action where disparities emerge

payload.text: [NCPS] shall establish clear expectations defining when artificial intelligence use is permitted, when unaided work is required, and how artificial intelligence assistance must be acknowledged.
Assessment practices shall emphasize reasoning, analysis, and evidence of student thinking.
Consistent with state guidance, [NCPS] shall not rely on artificial intelligence detection tools as the primary means of enforcing academic integrity, given their documented unreliability.
[NCPS] shall provide developmentally appropriate artificial intelligence literacy instruction aligned with Maryland's Digital Literacy and Computer Science standards.

Instruction shall be integrated across disciplines and grade levels and shall help students understand how artificial intelligence systems function, evaluate outputs for accuracy and bias, and use these tools ethically.

[NCPS]  shall  provide  role-specific  professional  learning  so  that  educators,  administrators, specialists,  and  support  staff  can  use  artificial  intelligence  safely,  ethically,  and  effectively.
Professional  learning shall emphasize  critical evaluation of artificial intelligence outputs, protection of student data, and recognition of when artificial intelligence use is inappropriate.
Artificial  intelligence  used  in  school  system  operations  shall  be  treated  as  a  higher-risk  use requiring caution, transparency, and continuous human oversight.
Operational artificial intelligence systems that affect student opportunities shall be evaluated for bias before adoption and monitored over time.
Artificial intelligence tools shall be vetted before adoption for educational value, data practices, accessibility, and legal compliance.

Vendor contracts shall limit data use, retention, and deletion; prohibit advertising, profiling, and unrelated model training; require disclosure of data practices; and ensure compliance with breach notification laws.

[NCPS]  shall  communicate  clearly  with  students,  families,  and  staff  about  what  artificial intelligence tools are used, what data are collected, how long data are retained, and when optout options apply, using accessible and culturally and linguistically responsive formats.
The Board directs the Superintendent to develop, maintain, and periodically review administrative regulations necessary to implement this policy.

The Superintendent shall designate a cross-functional team, including instructional, technology, legal, special education, multilingual learner, equity, and operational leadership, to guide artificial intelligence planning and oversight.
The Superintendent shall establish procedures for vetting and approving artificial intelligence tools, monitoring their use for bias and unintended effects, and addressing errors or harm.
payload.mechanism_stated: establish procedures for vetting and approving artificial intelligence tools

payload.text: The Superintendent shall report to the Board periodically on the implementation of this policy, including equity impacts and emerging risks.
